fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is addition of Ti, but the specified starting alloy is already nominally equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The hypothesis changes the baseline to Ti-free CoCrFeNi rather than treating the given CoCrFeNiTi alloy.
It omits the target high-energy ball-milling and spark-plasma-sintering intervention and its quantitative processing window.
It predicts a single-phase FCC structure, conflicting with the target nanocrystalline 83% FCC/17% BCC structure.
No quantitative hardness, strength, density, grain-size, or retained-plasticity prediction is given.
explanation: The cited paper validly supports Ti alloying of Ti-free CoCrFeNi and reports increased hardness and tensile strength, so the general compositional claim has some external support. However, it does not answer the posed problem because CoCrFeNiTi is already the starting composition. The proposed VHPS route, single-FCC mediator, generic core-effect mechanism, Ti-content boundary, and Ti-free baseline do not reconstruct the relevant HEBM-plus-SPS hypothesis. The falsification experiment is only broadly comparative and lacks specified milling/sintering conditions, phase-fraction or grain-size criteria, mechanical test parameters, and quantitative pass/fail predictions. It also fails to establish retention of favorable plasticity or machinability.
